title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page (23) gives a progress summary inside Grothendieck's 1986 'third version' of Analysis situs. There he tries to axiomatize a tame ('modérée') topology through abstract structures called 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set M of 'figures' carrying several relations:
- ≤, inclusion of figures;
- ≪, being an internal refinement or stratum;
- ∥, disjointness;
- a compatibility relation (written as a negated ≍ on the next page).
The 'lieux' L (loci) are the ≪-minimal elements, i.e. the elementary cells or points. Two flavours appear throughout: 'spac' (spatial ateliers, of the semialgebraic or o-minimal kind) and 'pol' (polyhedral ateliers).

Top of the page. This continues the implication bookkeeping of p.22, which records:
- (a) L2 + CL ⇔ L2 + C;
- (b) D0 + L1 + CL ⇒ L2;
- (c) L2 + L3 ⇒ D ⇒ D0.
Grothendieck first sets the divisibility axiom At L1 aside, then states a chain of implications:
- L1 + L2 + L3 + CL(spac) ⇔ D0 + L1 + L3 + CL(spac). The forward direction uses (c); the backward direction uses (b) to recover L2.
- This in turn ⇒ D + L1 + CL(spac) + C(spac), using (c) for D and (a) for C(spac).
- Hence the whole package L1, L2, L3, CL implies all the compatibility and disjunction axioms, in the 'spac' style and likewise in 'pol'. The side note reads: '…impliquent tous les axiomes de compatibilité — en supposant [les] styles "spac" — plus bien sûr At L1 lui-même'.
The practical upshot is that the 'conditional' axioms C, D, D0 can be replaced by axioms stated purely on the loci. This is exactly what p.24 exploits: in a special atelier satisfying CL, compatibility of figures is determined by a graph structure (the relation ∥) on the set L of minimal elements. Grothendieck then asks which conditions on (M, ≤, ≪, ∥|L) characterise such ateliers.

Main part: a recapitulation of the axiom system, excluding the existence-of-subdivision axioms. It is grouped by marginal braces.

(i) 'Grammar' axioms, split into a ≤ block and a ≪ block:
- At1: suprema of filtered families that have an upper bound.
- At2–At4: criteria for ≤, for compatibility and for ≪ that can be checked stratum by stratum.
- At5: a criterion for refinements between subfigures.
- At6: the axiom of the smallest stratum, i.e. refinements between strata X ≪ Y.
- At7: transitivity of internal refinements.

(ii) Compatibility and disposition axioms:
- At C: a criterion for compatibility of refinements of two figures.
- At D: a disposition criterion.
- At D0: stability of ∥ under ≪.
- These are ordered by C ⇒ D ⇒ D0.
- Special-case variants C(spac) and C(pol) are listed separately.

(iii) Existence axioms:
- At Fil: existence of filtered suprema of refinements, or (inserted) of locally finite families of refinements.
- At supp.: left as '…', unspecified.

(iv) Axioms concerning the loci:
- L1: divisibility.
- L2: disposition criterion via loci.
- L3: disposition axiom for loci.
- CL(spac) and CL(pol): compatibility criterion via loci.

The arrow from the 'Fil' box toward CL suggests that CL interacts with the existence of filtered refinements.
errors: The third line drops At L3, which is still needed downstream. As bookkeeping this is harmless, since the line only records consequences.
Every implication relies on the lemmas (a)–(e) of p.22, which are stated there without proof. The equivalences cannot be checked independently because the axioms are only named, not stated.

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatization of tame topology via 'ateliers': a poset of figures with inclusion ≤, internal refinement/stratification ≪ and disjointness/compatibility, with 'spatial' and 'polyhedral' variants
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; compare o-minimal structures, stratified spaces and the abstract poset/face-poset descriptions of regular cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s–1998). Tame topology programme: Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; the atelier axiomatics itself is unpublished (archive cote 156)

ideas.what: Reduction of compatibility and disjunction axioms to axioms on minimal elements (loci): L1+L2+L3+CL ⇒ C, D, D0
ideas.modern_name: Reconstructing a stratified or cell structure from its face poset plus an incidence/disjointness graph on vertices (cf. simplicial complexes determined by flag/clique data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorial topology (face posets of regular CW complexes: Björner and others)

ideas.what: Classification of axioms into 'grammar' axioms, compatibility/disposition axioms, existence axioms and locus axioms
ideas.modern_name: Structuring of an axiomatic theory (meta-level bookkeeping)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's abstract 'atelier' framework for tame topology has never been developed or compared in the literature with o-minimal structures or with combinatorial models of stratified spaces. Its main intended theorem is a characterization of special polyhedral ateliers by (M, ≤, ≪) plus a graph ∥ on the loci (posed on p.24). On this page it is still only a question.
missed.quote: At L1 + At L2 + At L3 + At CL(spac) ⇕ At D0 + At L1 + At L3 + At CL(spac) ⇓ At D + At L1 + At CL(spac) + At C(spac)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An order-theoretic axiomatization of tame figures could complement o-minimality, which is model-theoretic. It might also link to the combinatorial and exit-path descriptions of stratified spaces used in recent homotopy theory, such as Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix A and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a bookkeeping summary of axioms and of implications between them. It is of historical interest as evidence that Grothendieck built a detailed unpublished axiomatics for tame topology, but it contains no new theorem by itself.
transcription_corrections: Side note to the implication chain: likely '…impliquent tous les axiomes de compatibilité — en supposant [les] styles "spac" — plus bien sûr At L1 lui-même'.
Margin by the arrows: probably 'deux axiomes existentiels At D, At C(sp) et deux axiomes relatifs à L' rather than 'et sachant'.
At5 parenthesis: the image looks more like '(E⊂F, G⊂H, F≪G ⇒ E≪H)' or similar than 'P≤G ⇔ P≪G'. It is uncertain.
Marginal label of the middle group: 'axiomes de compatibilité, disposition'. Label of the first group: 'axiomes "de grammaire"', with a sub-label 'compar[aison] de ≤ et ≪'.
